source.title: Certified Circuits: Stability Guarantees for Mechanistic Circuits
source.authors: Alaa Anani; Tobias Lorenz; B. Schiele; Mario Fritz; Jonas Fischer

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether GPT-2 Small circuits preserve IOI task accuracy, but uses EAP-IG edge selection and dataset-deletion certification rather than the original head-level circuit analysis.
record.gate_note: The study reports circuit-restricted next-token accuracy for IOI and IOI-Hard circuits discovered on ID prompts and evaluated on ID and OOD prompts. These results bear on circuit sufficiency and transfer across the tested prompt settings. The paper cites the original IOI study but does not use its cited results as new evidence. Greater-Than and vision results do not test the IOI claim.
record.test_reason: The study uses IOI prompts on GPT-2 Small as a benchmark for its own certification wrapper around EAP-IG. Every IOI result compares certified EAP-IG edge circuits with uncalibrated EAP-IG circuits and the full model. It never identifies head classes or roles, never compares its circuits with the 26-head circuit, never ablates name movers, and covers no other model. The cACC numbers describe its own method's performance, not whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. On language, certified EAP-IG circuits match EAP-IG peak accuracy, which is saturated at 1.00 on all ID tasks. They use 38–80% fewer edges, except 2% fewer on OOD IOI-Hard. The one notable accuracy gain is on OOD IOI-Hard (0.91 vs 0.85). The authors present certification as giving provably stable, more compact circuits that generalize better to OOD.
record.recipe_differences: Uses EAP-IG edge attribution and randomized deletion smoothing with component abstention, then evaluates computation restricted to the selected edges. It does not reproduce the original head-level causal patching and ablation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported circuit accuracy varies with task and prompt split: IOI-Hard with OOD Q&A detours has lower cACC than the tested ID settings. The paper also compares EAP-IG and certified EAP-IG circuits.

fits_no_version.finding: On GPT-2 Small, EAP-IG edge circuits discovered on ID IOI prompts keep about 0.99–1.00 exact next-token accuracy on OOD prompts with place/object distractor clauses. On the authors' IOI-Hard Q&A-detour prompts, circuit accuracy (0.85 EAP-IG, 0.91 certified) exceeds the full model's 0.79 (Table 1, Fig. 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Edge-level attribution circuits for IOI in GPT-2 Small, found on standard prompts, preserve task accuracy under distractor-laden prompts, sometimes above the full model.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The relevant language results are reported as peak circuit accuracies without uncertainty estimates. The circuits are edge-level EAP-IG circuits, so the results do not directly validate the original 26-head circuit or its assigned head roles.
record.rows_left_out: Greater-Than results are omitted because they concern a different task, not IOI. Circuit-size comparisons are also omitted because they do not directly measure the IOI behavior or the named head roles. Vision results do not concern the claim's model or behavior.

untested.parts: The 26 heads, the 7 classes and their roles, and the faithfulness/completeness/minimality criteria are all untested. Only sufficiency of EAP-IG edge circuits is measured.
No name-mover ablation and no backup-head analysis.
GPT-2 Small only; no other models, sizes, checkpoints, or reuse of components.
No comparison of the recovered edges with the original circuit; EAP-IG vs certified EAP-IG is not a test of recovering the IOI circuit.
No variation of ablation type or metric on the IOI circuit. Zero-ablation with exact-match accuracy only, applied to the authors' own circuits.
OOD distractor prompts are used, but no analysis of whether the same components or heuristics carry IOI across formats. No name-order, template or more-names tests of the IOI circuit.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests'/T2 classification and its V1/V5/V6 labels are not justified. The paper never relates its edge circuits to the Wang et al. head classes. All rows are the study's own method versus its baseline, so they are relinked to none. The 'partial' states on R7/R8 misread the data: circuit accuracy exceeds the full model's 0.79. The language results have no uncertainty estimates, and certification hyperparameters were tuned per task and split, with the best configuration reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the original 26-head, 7-class circuit, the stated roles of its head classes, or its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria; it evaluates EAP-IG edge circuits instead.
The study does not ablate main name-mover heads or test whether backup heads take over.
It evaluates GPT-2 Small only and does not test whether the same circuit is present in other models, sizes, or checkpoints, or whether its components are reused for other tasks.
It does not compare alternative circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or faithfulness metrics for recovery of the original circuit.

The study tests circuit-restricted accuracy across ID and OOD prompt settings and compares EAP-IG with certified circuits, but does not compare ablation types or multiple behavioral metrics, or establish that the original circuit explains only part of IOI.
The study tests ID prompts and task-specific OOD distractor prompts, including IOI-Hard, but does not systematically test name order, multiple templates, or more names.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 Small IOI circuits, ID prompts and the tested OOD object/place distractor prompts
reader_labels.reason: EAP-IG and certified EAP-IG circuit-restricted computation reaches 1.00 cACC on ID prompts; on OOD IOI prompts the reported values are 0.99 and 1.00 (R1-R4). This supports circuit sufficiency in these settings, not the claimed head classes or exact original circuit.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: IOI ID prompts and OOD object/place distractor prompts
reader_labels.reason: Circuit-restricted accuracy is at or near 1.00 in both prompt settings for the reported IOI circuits (R1-R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: IOI-Hard OOD prompts with Q&A detours
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy is incomplete for both circuits: EAP-IG reaches 0.85 and certified EAP-IG reaches 0.91 (R7-R8), despite the improvement from certification.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: IOI OOD prompts with object/place distractors
reader_labels.reason: Circuits discovered on ID prompts retain near-saturated or saturated IOI accuracy on the tested OOD prompt construction (R3-R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: IOI-Hard OOD prompts with Q&A detours
reader_labels.reason: Circuit-restricted accuracy is 0.85 for EAP-IG and 0.91 for the certified circuit, so preservation is incomplete in this harder prompt setting (R7-R8).
